messages.body_plain:
Dear all,

I have been trying to run the following model:

model2 = lmer(log(RT)~Group*A*B*C+(1|name)+ (1+A*B*C|subject),data=dtc)

but R kept running for a very long time without ever giving me an output.

So I tried running:

model2 = lmer(log(RT)~Group*A*B*C+(1|name)+ (1+A+B+C|subject),data=dtc)

although this is not exactly what I want.
This is the error I got:

Warning message:
In function (fn, par, lower = rep.int(-Inf, n), upper = rep.int(Inf,  :
  failure to converge in 10000 evaluations

And then when I type summary I get:

[1] "Asymptotic covariance matrix A is not positive!"

In the results for the fixed effects, I have NA in lieu of some of the p
values and it seems to be particularly related to factor B. The contrast
for Factor B (which is in fact stimulus position) is:
> contrasts(dtc$B)
  R
L 0
R 1

Also, when I tried to get confidence intervals using lsmean, I again got
the "Asymptotic covariance matrix A is not positive!" error.

I would be very very grateful if someone could help me out here.


Note that I am able to get an output when running this model on error rates:

model1e =
glmer(correct~Group*A*B*C+(1|name)+(1+A*B*C|subject),data=dt,family=binomial)

although I also get the "failure to converge" error...


Best,

Stephanie

messages.body_plain:
Dear Stephanie,

You could try adding the following argument:

model2 = lmer( log(RT) ~ Group*A*B*C +(1|name) +(1+A+B+C|subject),
     data=dtc,
     control=lmerControl(optCtrl=list(maxfun=50000))
     )

This argument sets the max number of iterations to 50000 instead of the 
default 10000. This has worked well for me in the past, for models with 
many random effects. Hope this helps!

Best, Hugo Quené

messages.body_plain:
Just another shot in the dark: are you excluding RTs on error trials? (I'm
guessing yes.)  If so, have you checked on how much data you have left?
 While sparse data is not necessarily a problem, I often see model
convergence problems when there is just not much data in particular cells
(like maybe some people don't have any data left in one cell or another).
 Unfortunately I don't have any great suggestions for what to do about it,
but maybe this would help isolate the problem.  Depending on your data,
some kinds of other missing-data treatments (like some kind of imputation
method) might be reasonable, and might at least give you enough to get the
model to fit.

good luck!
-scott
